propositions: Plans assert that named modules provide or lack capabilities when those assertions are refuted by the actual code, causing agents to build missing capabilities or unnecessarily rebuild existing ones.

The new asserted-capability criterion detects when a plan makes a capability-surface claim about a named module that is not grounded in the actual codebase (either claiming a capability exists when it does not, or claiming it must be built when it already exists).

The criterion is registered as advisory and code-grounded in the G6/E4 rubric family, plugs into existing pass machinery without core changes, and ships with registry entries, routing configuration, and rubric documentation.

The bounded sanity check demonstrates the probe fires on all 3 E1-verified false-assertion cases and correctly does not fire on clean control plans, with one advisory false-fire recorded as dogfood data for future promotion to blocking.
The criterion auto-flows into the standing criterion-effectiveness recorder with zero per-criterion wiring and follows the established advisory→blocking promotion gate protocol.
Registration is validated via canonical-list membership, non-orphan status in routing and guide sections, and deterministic unit tests on registration invariants and prompt contracts.
